title: Gloomhaven: Jaws of the Lion - Take a Look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ou7NGOVJ8Pc

Daniel (@dungeondive) finally puts Gloomhaven on the channel, as seven numbered claims. Six praise Jaws of the Lion. The seventh: he still doesn't like Gloomhaven.

The praise is substantial. He calls it the new gold standard for onboarding. A component sheet sorts everything before you start, and the learn-to-play guide reinforces as it teaches: in the second scenario, an enemy card simply says the vermlings act exactly as they did in the first. He wishes Jerry Hawthorne's games had a guide like it. Playing solo with Hatchet and Voidwarden, with full communication, fixes his complaint about the semi-competitive table. The small box sets up fast, the single-city setting evokes Fritz Leiber's Fafhrd and the Gray Mouser, and the spiral-bound map books have him imagining a crawl built entirely from four flip-books. Above all, a kid could buy this at Target, and he suspects it will be someone's HeroQuest in 30 years.

The objections remain. Burning cards to rest means each mission starts exciting and ends with dwindling options, a story told backwards. Armor usable once per rest makes no thematic sense, the pursuit of balance costs the fun, and with no random encounters or NPCs it's a tactical combat game rather than a dungeon crawl. He may give it to his nephews.

----

Daniel recommends a game he doesn't enjoy playing. Is there a game you'd press on others even though it isn't for you?
